x: All three statements are correct. India has 11 classical languages; Telugu (2008), Marathi and Bengali are all classical languages; and Pali and Prakrit are the only classical languages that lie outside the Eighth Schedule.

The three-language formula (NPE 1968) remains a live language-policy dispute (Jun 2026). The other options are false: Tamil (2004) is still the first classical language, regional languages have not been abolished from education, and Urdu remains AP's second official language.

APNRT, the AP Non-Resident Telugu Society, ran the help desk for Telugus stranded in the Gulf (Mar 2026). The other pairs are wrong: IOM publishes the World Migration Report, the NSO/MoSPI runs the Nationwide Migration Survey, and the NRT networks in 148 countries are run by the AP government.
